description: Executable invariants of the event build. Each invariant restates what its source requirements already require, independent of implementation strategy, and names the tests that must check it: property tests (random command and provider-reply sequences against the save process and the stateful fake), model tests (the state machines in state-machines.json), negative tests (forged or illegal inputs must fail), and mutation checks (reverting the guard must make a named test fail, DCC-005). Test identities follow the plan's convention; a test proves nothing by being named. A clause backed only by an owner decision request is marked with that request and is not normative until approved.
testConvention: dotnet:Causa.Invariants.<Kind>.<INV id without dash>.<case>; playwright:invariants/<INV id>.spec.js > <case> [chromium] for browser cases

invariants.statement: An investigation is Saved only after GitHub returned the commit for that exact mutation and a re-read at that commit returned exactly the written bytes, or reconciliation found this save's marker on a commit holding exactly those bytes.

tests.checks: for random sequences of edits, saves and fake replies (including forged commit oids and mismatched read-backs), Saved occurs only immediately after a matching read-back or marker reconciliation
with the read-back comparison removed (compare with itself) a named test fails

invariants.statement: A reply to a request the tab has superseded never changes the state, the base head or the unsaved changes; in particular a stale or reordered response cannot overwrite newer local state or reach Saved.

tests.checks: permuting the delivery order of replies to superseded loads, refreshes, conflict re-reads and reconciliation reads leaves the final state equal to delivering only the current replies
Rehearsal 7 third-review E1: a late read of head h1 after a re-read at h2 is dropped and the other writer's change survives reapply
Rehearsal 7 third-review E2: a refresh requested at base b1 that completes after a save moved the tab to b2 is dropped

invariants.statement: An uncertain remote outcome is never automatically classified as failure or conflict: a lost answer leads to Unknown commit outcome, and only reconciliation decides it; a network failure is never a stale head or a conflict.

tests.checks: losing the answer at any point (before or after the fake applies the mutation) never yields Conflict or Save failed without a reconciliation result that justifies it
Rehearsal 7 KD-018: an applied commit whose answer was lost and that reconciliation does not yet see is never reported as a conflict caused by this save's own commit

invariants.statement: Per tab at most one commit mutation is in flight; per save request at most four mutations and at most three automatic reconciliation reads at least 2, 4 and 8 seconds apart (plus one per offline-to-online change); under total network failure at most four mutations and four reconciliation reads in 60 seconds; a save that failed before sending is not retried automatically.

tests.checks: request counts and spacing under random failure schedules, with a virtual clock

invariants.statement: Every mutation is one createCommitOnBranch whose expectedHeadOid is a head this tab read from GitHub in its session, touching only paths under the investigation's own prefix, carrying a write marker unique across tabs, devices and page loads; no forced ref update, per-file write or headless write exists.

tests.checks: every mutation the fake records satisfies the shape; markers never repeat across simulated tabs, reloads and reconnects (Rehearsal 7 F5)

invariants.statement: No investigation content, unsaved change, save state, branch head, write marker or credential is written to any browser store or cross-tab channel, and no Web Locks API is used.

tests.id: playwright:invariants/INV-06.spec.js > every store empty of investigation content [chromium]
tests.checks: after edits, saves, conflicts and offline periods every browser store is inspected

invariants.statement: Unsaved user changes remain in tab memory, visible and saveable by a new request through every recoverable failure the baseline names: offline, stale head, rebase limit, conflict, unknown outcome and provider refusal. They are dropped only by an explicit, confirmed discard or by the tab ending.

tests.checks: for random failure sequences the multiset of unsaved commands is unchanged except by confirmed discard or a confirmation that saved them
Rehearsal 7 F2: refresh is refused, and a completing load is dropped, while the investigation holds unsaved changes, a save in flight or a conflict

invariants.statement: No action replaces the GitHub version with the tab's version; conflict resolution offers only review, reapply through the engine, and confirmed discard.

tests.checks: every reachable SM-CONFLICT state offers no overwrite action

invariants.statement: After any sequence of saves, rebases, reconciliations and conflict resolutions by any number of tabs, every other writer's commit remains reachable from the branch head.

tests.checks: random interleavings of three simulated tabs and an external writer against the stateful fake
live PAT-02 reachability check (already bound by the plan)

invariants.statement: Two tabs are independent: a change in one never appears in another until it is saved to GitHub and the other loads it from GitHub; correctness never depends on cross-tab coordination.

tests.id: playwright:invariants/INV-10.spec.js > tabs independent with and without navigator.locks [chromium]
tests.checks: PAT-01 and PAT-11 shape with random edit orders

invariants.statement: Every file set read or written satisfies the frozen causa-storage v1.0.0 contract: schema-valid manifest, events and snapshot; digests (including eventsSha256) match; contract-fixed values equal the contract's; the snapshot state equals the state replayed from the event history through the F# engine. A file set that fails any check is refused, never partially rendered.

tests.checks: for each check (schema, each digest including eventsSha256, each contract-fixed value, snapshot-equals-replay, required fields) a forged file set that only that check rejects is refused; removing the check makes the test fail (Rehearsal 7 surviving eventsSha256 mutant)
every file set the application writes re-reads and replays to its snapshot

invariants.statement: Every domain change, including each command re-decided during reapply, is decided by the F# domain engine; refused commands are never applied.

tests.checks: reapply result equals folding the unsaved commands through decide/evolve at the GitHub version; refused commands carry the engine's reason

invariants.statement: Each investigation has exactly one of the seven save states; each page shows the state of the investigation it displays; the workspace summary never contradicts the investigations it counts.

tests.checks: for two investigations driven into different states the header, page and summary agree with the machine

invariants.statement: The words saved, synced, stored and safe describe an investigation only in Saved, and no copy promises local, queued or later saving.

tests.checks: every message the save-state projection can produce, for every state and cause, is scanned

invariants.statement: The implementation agent cannot certify its own acceptance: independent-acceptance evidence comes from a party that did not author the change, and agent-authored accepted fields are advisory.

tests.checks: a fresh reviewer's record at the exact SHA
requirements-compiler verify-plan refuses a review attestation whose author is the implementing agent

invariants.statement: A passing build does not imply requirements acceptance: acceptance is computed from evidence for every P0 obligation and the deployed acceptance job of the exact SHA.

tests.checks: a ledger with green CI but missing obligation evidence yields a non-accepting verdict

invariants.statement: Every acceptance claim references evidence produced from the exact accepted commit; evidence for another SHA, or from an earlier rehearsal, never counts.

tests.checks: verify-plan with --trusted-source-sha different from the evidence SHA is INVALID

invariants.statement: A test that was not implemented, not run, skipped or failed is never reported as PASS; missing verification is BLOCKED or UNKNOWN.

tests.checks: a ledger row NOT_RUN for a bound test leaves its obligation unverified

invariants.statement: The acceptance contract changes only through an operator-written approval record: an implementation agent cannot amend, exclude or re-derive an obligation because its code fails.

tests.checks: an amendment without a matching operator record makes verify-plan INVALID (UNAUTHORIZED-AMENDMENT)
requirements-compiler v4 --check fails when acceptance/ differs from the frozen digest in freeze-manifest.json

invariants.statement: The candidate contains no application source, test or script copied from Causa or an earlier rehearsal repository (indy-init-rehearsal-001 to indy-init-rehearsal-006 in the baseline; ODR-V4-02 proposes adding indy-init-rehearsal-007). The comparison is run by a verifier permitted to read those repositories, never by the implementing agent (Rehearsal 7 KD-009).

tests.checks: PAT-13 comparison against indy-init-rehearsal-001..006, run and recorded by the independent verifier at the exact final SHA
the same comparison recorded for PERSIST-026's copy ban by the independent verifier

invariants.statement: The credential exists only in tab memory, is sent only in the Authorization header over HTTPS to the GitHub API (or the site's own origin in tests), never appears in URLs, logs, screenshots, traces or artifacts; every read and write needs it; write permission is never inferred from a successful read; the read and write tokens never fall back to each other.

tests.checks: Rehearsal 7 F14: the credential is never sent to a plaintext or other host

tests.id: playwright:invariants/INV-21.spec.js > no credential in storage, URL or artifact [chromium]
tests.checks: stores, URLs, console, screenshots and traces scanned for the test token

invariants.statement: Provider answers are classified from their typed content into distinct causes (stale head in every form GitHub sends, network failure, authentication, permission, rate limit including secondary limits, validation); a rate limit is never reported as a missing permission and a moved head never as a refusal.

tests.checks: classification of every recorded GitHub answer form, including STALE_DATA, FORBIDDEN 'is at <oid> but expected <oid>' (Rehearsal 7 KD-022) and HTTP 403 secondary rate-limit messages (KD-020)
three simultaneous live commits to the test repository; every refusal GitHub returns is classified as a stale head

invariants.statement: A CI step that runs a check cannot report success when the check failed: every step runs with errexit and pipefail, and every PAT and browser suite runs to completion so that each test yields its own result.

tests.checks: conditor ci-policy check on the rehearsal repository at kickoff and on every candidate (DCC-013); Rehearsal 7 D-01 pipefail defect and WebKit stop-after-first-failure (9 NOT_RUN)

invariants.statement: Every save-state action and recovery path (Save, Retry, Check again, Reconnect, conflict review, reapply, discard and its confirmation) is operable by keyboard alone, has an accessible name, moves focus into any dialog it opens and returns focus when the dialog closes, and announces its result through the live regions PERSIST-030 requires; every colour comes from a Forma 0.12.0 token that exists.

tests.id: playwright:invariants/INV-24.spec.js > save-state and conflict actions by keyboard and screen reader [webkit]
tests.checks: keyboard-only operation, accessible names, focus into and back from the discard confirmation and Reconnect, live-region announcements, in WebKit (iPad target)
every Forma custom property the stylesheet references exists in Forma 0.12.0's published token set (Rehearsal 7 post-deadline finding: four nonexistent token names)

invariants.statement: A refused credential and a conflict whose GitHub version is deleted or unverifiable are also recoverable: re-authentication keeps every unsaved change, and an unresolvable conflict offers an export of the unsaved commands without writing to GitHub or browser storage.

tests.checks: a revoked token followed by Reconnect with a new token keeps every unsaved change and saves it
a deleted or unverifiable GitHub version leaves the conflict with an export action and the work kept
